explication: Go Cryptography is a collection of supplementary cryptographic primitives, protocol implementations, certificate tooling, and secure transport libraries. The principal workflow is: an application invokes a package API, the package parses or exchanges protocol data, applies cryptographic operations, and returns authenticated messages, keys, sessions, certificates, or trust roots. Major independent branches include SSH, ACME, OpenPGP, OTR, password/key derivation, AEAD/signatures, and certificate-root handling. The graph reflects the tree, README, and sampled source; unsampled package relationships are intentionally omitted.
